mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is always active and does not require a specific trigger condition.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate within a month signals aggressive monetary tightening, which immediately pressures equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in payroll employment signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points and PAYEMS rises by at least 50,000 over the prior month, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a sustained increase in housing starts and retail sales signals strong consumer demand, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes (defined as UNRATE below 5.0% and FEDFUNDS above 3.0%), the joint signal of HOUST rising by at least 1% and RSAFS rising by at least 0.5% over the prior month fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index indicates expanding manufacturing output, which correlates with stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. This mechanism is always active and does not require a specific trigger condition.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods when INDPRO has increased by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in the Consumer Price Index within a month signals rising inflation, which triggers fears of monetary tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and CPI signals a 'stagflation' regime, which immediately pressures equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25 percentage points and CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.2 percentage points within a month, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high labor market tightness regimes (UNRATE below 4.5% and PAYEMS growth above 100,000), a further decline in unemployment and continued payroll growth signals robust consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In high labor market tightness regimes (UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS growth > 100,000), the signal of UNRATE falling and PAYEMS rising fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
